pages.title: Data transfer Instructions
pages.text:
Data transfer Instructions:

Move destination, source
Source can be register, memory location, immediate operand.
both cant be memory location at the same time.
stack operations:
Push AX - Pop AX - Pusha AX - PopA AX
AX can be any register or memory location
address transfer:
LEA register, source
LEA BX, [DI] <-> mov BX, offset [DI]
To get the address of DI "first char" and store it in BX

Arithmetic Instructions:

-ADD destination, source
with add operation we can add byte to byte or word to word like:
ADD AX, CX / AX = AX + CX / But ADD AL, BL is X
ADD AL, CL / AL = AL + CL
byte to word is wrong
8 bits 16 bits
I / Carry flag CF=1 then add
-ADC AX, BL -> AX = AX + BL + 1 / if CF=1
-INC source: increase register or source by 1
if AX=8 INC AX -> AX=9
-AAA -> It correct the content of AL

For Subtraction:

-SUB Destination, source Same as ADD
SUB AX, 4H -> AX = AX - 4H
-DEC source: decrease Source by 1
-NEG source: change the sign of the source (opposite sign)

pages.title: IT2207 - SBB and Arithmetic Instructions
pages.text:
IT2207 (2) 16.5.2025

SBB destination, source : Subtract with Borrow/carry
Like if the Carry Flag CF=1 it decrement the answer by 1
Ex: Mov AX, 12H } first we make AX = 12H
SCF } this change the nts of CF from 0 to 1
SBB AX, 5 } subtract AX = AX - 5 - 1 = 6H

CMP destination, source : Compare two specific bytes or words and do an instruction according to the result
CMP AX, 7H } this compare AX with 7 by subtracting them from each other
JNZ end; } if not zero jump to end.

for multiplication:
-MUL source: it multiply byte by byte or word by word.
1. if source is 1byte then AL is multiplied by it and stored in AX
2. if source is word then AX is multiplied by it and stored in DX:AX
(DX is upper) (AX is lower)
-IMUL source:
Same as MUL but it consider signs

For Division:
-DIV source: it divides word by byte or double-word by word
if source is 1 byte, AX is divided by source and quotient = AL & remainder = AH

pages.title: Variable declaration and Assembly I/O
pages.text:
if source is 1 word, (DX, AX) is divided by source,
and AX = quotient DX = remainder
-IDIV it is signed division instruction

Variable declaration in assembly:

DB: Define byte (8 bits) ; x db 2 (uninitialized variable)
DW: Define word (16 bits) / X dw 5 Y dw 2
DD: Define double word (32 bits)
DP: 6 bits
DQ: Define Quad word (64 bits)

Read/Input Variables:

To enter a character with the keyboard we do:
* Mov AH, 1 -> The function 1
* int 21h -> interrupt 21
The input is stored in AL. And the number is stored as a character to use it as a number:
- Sub AL, 48 OR Sub AL, '0'
Mov AH, 7
int 21h

Write or Display:

Mov DL, 'A' } You move the character you want to display to DL and then do this.
Mov AH, 2 }
int 21h } we can read only one digit at a time

Display a message:

* Mov DX, offset variable or LEA DX, variable
mov ah, 9 -> to display a message
int 21h

pages.title: IT2207 - Conditions and Logical Instructions
pages.text:
IT2207 (3) 17.5.2025

If, else condition:

we use cmp to solve if-else in assembly
cmp source, destination to get the result of cmp then
[ Jxy address of Label ] jump to address of Label
jl: jump if less, jle: jump if less or equal, je: jump if equal
jne: jump if not equal, jg: jump if greater, jge: jump if greater or equal, jnz: jump if not equal zero, jz: jump if equal zero
If we need to use jump without any condition we use jmp address of Label

Logical instructions:

-Not source: convert all the bits in a byte or word ex. 00110110 -> 11001001
-And destination, source : do AND operation on all bits
AH = 1001 1111 and AL, CL = 0000 1011
CL = 0000 1011
-OR destination, source : OR operation on bits
-XOR destination, source : XOR operation on bits
if you have trouble understanding this check page 5, week 3

Shift instruction:

-SHL destination, count (shift left)
It moves the most left bit to ... AL = 10110110 -> SHL AL, 5
The left and add zero at ...
the beginning and add the ...
moved bit as CF
-SHR destination, count (shift right)
same as SHL but in the other direction

pages.title: Shift and Rotate Instructions, Loops
pages.text:
-SAR source, count (shift Arithmetic right)
would the new bit according to AL = 10111001
the sign of the number, if it is negative SAR AL, 3
it starts and adds 1s else it add 0s AL = 11110111
-SAL destination, count (shift arithmetic left)
Same as SAR
Rotate instruction:
-Rol destination, count (Rotate left)
it rotate the bits in a byte or word ex. 10110111
so the left bit become the right and Rol AL, 1 -> 01101111
it is stored added to the CF also AL = 01101111 -> CF=1
-RoR destination, count (Rotate right)
Same as Rol
-RCL destination, count (Rotate through Carry Left)
In this instruction the first left bit CF=0
is stored in the CF and the previous CF=1
CF is added as the first right bit CF=0
-RCR
Same as RCL

Loop

-for: cmp cl, 4
jg end loop
add s, cl
inc cl
jmp for
end loop:
while: cmp si, 4
jg endwhile
add s, si
inc si
jmp while
end while:

pages.title: IT2209 - Propositions and Logic
pages.text:
IT2209: (1) 19.5.2025

Propositions: can be written p, q, r... and it is a propositional statement
Logical connections:
-And (AND / ^) : add two propositions and it is true when both are true
-or (v) : will be true if either p or q are true
-If then (->) : if p true then q should be true - called implies
-If and only if (<->) : this is true when both p and q are the same either true or false
-Negation - Not (~):

Tautologies & consistency:

-Tautology iff v(θ) = T with all θ any formula (|=)
-consistent iff v(θ) = T for one θ where it is true
-inconsistent iff v(θ) = F for all θ (is called contradiction)
Logical consequence: θ |= λ => if v(θ)=T then v(λ)=T
Logical equivalences: θ == λ iff v(θ)=Q=λ and λ |= θ
* Page 59 in pdf for memorize (the last one rule in both columns are True)
Note: |= (tautology)
|- (logical consequence)

Semantic Tableau system:

~~p | p ^ q | p v q | p -> q | p <-> q
p | p
q | p | q | ~p | q | ...

pages.title: Rules of Inference and Resolution
pages.text:
Branch is closed if there is X & ~X in the same root.
Rules of inference:
Modus Ponens (law of detachment - mode that affirms):
if a conditional statement and its hypothesis are true
then the conclusion must also be true
p -> q -> conditional statement
p -> hypothesis
∴ q -> conclusion
Important table page 72 (Rules of inference)
-Satisfiability (SAT) and Propositional resolution
p -> q
q -> r
∴ p -> r

Literal is : p or ~p or ~q
clause is : p or ~p or p v q v r or {p}, {~p}, {p, q}
Conversion to clausal
- p v q -> {p, q}
- p ^ q -> {p}, {q}
the empty clause is unsatisfiable
Proof by refutation or contradiction:
Γ |= A iff Γ U {~A} is unsatisfiable
to prove that Γ logical consequence of A we should
take the negation of the conclusion (~A) and prove that
it leads to an empty clause.

How to prove:

{p -> q, q -> r} |= p -> r?
1- Convert this to clausal:
p -> q => {~p, q} (1)
q -> r => {~q, r} (2)
~(p -> r) => {p}, {~r} (3)
Then number them
and last derive them from each other

pages.title: IT2207 - Processor Control Instructions
pages.text:
IT2207 (4) 23.5.2025

Processor control instructions:

STC : Set Carry Flag to 1
STD : Set direction Flag to 1
STI : Set Interrupt Flag to 1
CLC : Clear Carry Flag to 0
CLD : Clear direction Flag to 0
CLI : Clear interrupt Flag to 0
CMC : Complement CF
Note: JNC means if CF = 0, JNS means if SF = 0
SF: get the bit in the MSB, after an operation (add, sub) so we can determine the sign of a number
PF: if the number of 1 bits is even then it is set to 1, if the number is odd then it is cleared to 0
AF: contains the carry bit from the fourth bit to the fifth bit

Loop Instructions:

First we should define CX (count) the number of repetition and then start the loop ex for:
Loop for
and the CX Value will automatically decrease by 1 each loop without do that manually
Do - while loop:
same as for but use do ----
Loop do

Array:

A db 10 dup(0) , create an array A of 10 elements and fill them with 0
A db 10, 2, 7, 6 to create array
A dw 2, 5, 12
IMP: only SI & DI can be used to indicate an element in array A[SI], A[DI]
to move to a new line when display use new line db 10, 13, '$'
